title: I was able to catch one of the final performances of Les Mis at Radio...
transcript: I'm gonna be so honest, I had no intention of seeing Les Mis at Radio City Music Hall. I mean, I have seen Les Mis so many times, and the fact that it was just a concert production and not fully staged, it was hard for me to get excited about it, especially at the very high price point that they were charging. But once performances started, I was hearing really great things and the FOMO kind of took over. So I splurged on a ticket, and, yeah, it kind of did live up to the hype. And what I realised is that Les Mis is a show that is just always better. The larger the orchestra, the larger the cast. It is such an epic musical and such a lush score, and seeing it performed with a full orchestra, a cast of over 40 people, there really is nothing like it. Add on top of that, a cast that includes so many Les Mis alumni, some in new parts, like Samantha Barks, famously Eponine on stage and screen, now playing the role of Fantine. Philip Quast, a long time Javert, now playing the Bishop. And Rob Madge, a former Gavroche, now playing a small but memorable role. In the ensemble, you also have Matt Lucas as Thenardier, Jak Yarrow as Marius. And then at my performance, Valjean was played by Killian Donnelly, and Javert was played by Bradley Jaden, who has been dubbed by the internet as “Hot Javert” for a reason. but he is also truly unhinged in this role. Like I have never seen a Javert this cracked. But it is truly just an all star cast across the board. And while yes, I missed some of the larger staging moments and the iconic turntable, which sadly hasn't been a part of Les Miserables for a while now, this was still undeniably one of the best ways to experience the show. And the score. Seeing musical theatre done at this scale is so rare and it really reminded me just how good the show is.
